focus: /doctor:ci command surface: registration contract, validator-forced mode split, scaffold constraints from gate-inputs, ownership split with sk-code-ci
answeredQuestions: What should a /doctor:ci command do, how is it made safe, and who owns it?

graphEvents.label: What should /doctor:ci do, how is it made safe, and who owns it?

J1 requires manifest, router table and presentation parity

label: A /doctor:ci route is a six-surface change: _routes.yaml route entry with trigger_phrases; the owning router markdown with its target table; assets/<target>.yaml; assets/<command>-presentation.txt; a row in doctor-setup-presentation.txt; and scoring-compatibility.json activation entries in BOTH the typescript and python lists (a bridge without one stays inactive), followed by reruns of derive-command-bridges.cjs, route-validate.sh and doctor-phrase-reach.cjs; plus README.txt's group count, doctor command table and Ten command files sentence, which all go stale.

Route validator rule K1 fails any route marked mutating: read-only whose YAML declares a write, and E1 pins the mutation class to {read-only, add-only, mutates}; therefore /doctor:ci cannot be one route that both lists and toggles, and must be at least list and check as read-only, toggle and customize as mutates, and scaffold as add-only. /doctor:git already splits hooks and standards (mutates) from setup (read-only) the same way.

Validator J1 asserts target-set parity between the route manifest, each router's target table and the presentation file, and G1/G2 require trigger phrases; so every new /doctor:ci target must appear in ci.md's execution-target table and in doctor-setup-presentation.txt in the same commit or route-validate.sh fails the build.

A workflow emitted by /doctor:ci scaffold is constrained by gate-inputs: check-gate-inputs.sh requires every literal .opencode path a workflow runs to resolve, flags any escaped single-root literal such as \.opencode/ that lacks \.skilled/, and requires every path filter to name both roots; gate-inputs.yml itself copes by selecting the root with a sentinel (root=.skilled; [ -f "$root/skills/system-spec-kit/SKILL.md" ] || root=.opencode). A template with a literal .opencode run path turns the repository's own gate-inputs workflow red.

No automated workflow-to-README parity check was found: .github/scripts/ contains only check-gate-inputs.sh and its tests, and the README states each workflow owes a contents row and a push/pull-request coverage row as a convention. INFERRED from directory-level absence, not proven; what would confirm it is a repository-wide grep for a script parsing .github/workflows/*.yml against README.md.

The env doctor is the confirmed-write precedent /doctor:ci toggle must copy: the router owns argument parsing and asset loading only; the workflow reads its inventory live at invocation time instead of copying the list into any file, displays read-only set/unset state per source, shows the exact proposed line and destination, writes only after an explicit yes, treats --dry-run as the same preview without writing, and re-reads the changed file before its final status. For repository variables the analogous shape is print the gh variable set line, execute on yes, re-read and report the difference.

doctor-setup.yaml's read-only invariant (read_only true, allowed_targets empty, forbidden_targets "**/*", every leg in check-only form, a failing leg prints the repair command and never repairs) plus its leg taxonomy (PASS, DEGRADED for a real but non-failing exit such as sk-git exit 3, SKIP for an absent prerequisite, FAIL with a repair command, ERROR for a crash) is the contract /doctor:ci list and check must reuse; the umbrella runs every leg even after one fails.

Advisor routing for the new command is derivable but not automatic: derive-command-bridges.cjs requires a doctor bridge's id to equal its inventoryId, requires every inventoryId to name a known inventory entry and be unique per platform, and a bridge routes only once scoring-compatibility.json activates it in both the typescript and python lists; so /doctor:ci needs five command-doctor-ci-<target> ids and ten activation entries, with lead_phrases only where the doctor must outrank a passing skill.

Ownership splits along the artifact boundary: /doctor:ci owns inspection, toggling and customization (list, check, toggle, customize); sk-code-ci owns the standards and the workflow template; scaffold is the single seam, a doctor route that writes a file whose content comes from the sk-code-ci template rather than YAML embedded in the doctor workflow, mirroring how the env doctor reads its inventory live instead of copying it. It does not belong in sk-git, whose doctor route is scoped to .git config and .sk-git/ standards. INFERRED design recommendation.

direction: One /doctor:ci route that lists, toggles and scaffolds behind a single mode flag
reason: Validator rule K1 fails a mutating: read-only route whose YAML declares any write, and E1 constrains the mutation class to one value per route, so a combined route cannot be both an honest read-only listing and a writer; the family's own /doctor:git already splits mutates from read-only routes.

sk-git's doctor surface is scoped to git config hook gates and .gitconfig/.sk-git standards; CI workflow state is neither, and the sk-code router forbids editing workflow YAML while executing an sk-code command, so the authoring contract belongs to sk-code-ci while the inspection contract belongs to the doctor family.
